summary: A reading site: an editorial magazine or journal with issues, topics and long reads, or an engineering / technical blog with code samples, tags and a keyboard-first post index. Home, the archive and the article page carry it; author and about pages are optional.

pages.purpose: Show what the publication is and what is new, and get the reader into one piece quickly.

sections.purpose: The masthead: current issue or theme with its table of contents (magazine), or a plain-text intro beside the latest post (technical blog).
alternatives: hero: a full-width masthead with the publication name and one-line promise
fields: Current issue number, date and theme (magazine)
Latest post: title, date, reading time, author
sections.notes: A technical blog can show an excerpt of the latest post as code; a terminal-style typing eyebrow is optional and must render as plain text without motion.

sections.purpose: The lead piece large: image, topic, title, dek, author and reading time.
fields: Lead article title, dek, topic, author, reading time

sections.purpose: Latest pieces with topic chips, or a post index read like a log: date, title, tags, minutes.
alternatives: list-layout: a dense mono post index with '/' to filter and j / k to move, for a technical blog
fields: Per post: title, dek or summary, topic / tags, author, date, reading time, cover image (magazine)
sections.notes: If keyboard shortcuts are offered, document them on the page and ignore them while typing in a field.

sections.purpose: Topics with post counts and the authors, each opening the archive filtered.
fields: Authors: name, role, short bio, photo

sections.purpose: A most-read list beside an editor's letter (magazine).
Subscribe by email, with the cadence and an RSS link.
alternatives: form-01: an inline email field that validates in place and confirms without leaving the page
fields: What subscribers get and how often

pages.purpose: Every piece, filterable by topic, tag, author, year or a search, paged.

sections.purpose: Title and how many pieces there are.
Search plus topic / tag / author filters.
sections.notes: Keep the filter in the URL (e.g. a hash per topic) so topic chips and author links elsewhere open the archive pre-filtered and back / forward keep working. Announce the result count in a polite live region.

sections.purpose: The matching pieces, grouped by year for a long archive, with paging.
alternatives: empty-state: when a filter matches nothing, offering to clear it
fields: Posts with title, summary, topic, author, date, reading time

pages.purpose: One piece, comfortable to read to the end: header, body with notes, code or figures, the author and what to read next.

sections.purpose: Topic, title, dek, author, date, updated date and reading time; cover image for a magazine.
fields: Cover image with alt text and credit

sections.purpose: A reading-progress bar with minutes left for long reads.
The text, with footnotes as side notes on wide screens (endnotes on narrow), figures, call-outs, tables and code samples.
alternatives: tabs: code samples in several languages that switch together across the page
table: benchmark or data tables with a caption
alert: an aside or warning call-out
section-nav: margin contents for a long technical post
fields: Figures with captions and alt text
sections.notes: Footnote numbers jump to the side note when visible, else the endnote; both link back; notes use role="note". Code blocks scroll sideways inside their own box, have a copy button with a status message, and a language choice that is one setting for the page.

sections.purpose: Who wrote it, with a link to their other pieces.
fields: Author name, role, short bio, photo

sections.purpose: Subscribe at the end of the piece.
fields: What subscribers get and how often

pages.purpose: Who publishes it, editorial policy, contributors and how to pitch or get in touch.

sections.purpose: What the publication is for and who is behind it.
Editorial standards, corrections and pitching guidelines.

content: Publication name, one-line description and publisher
Topics or tags with short descriptions
Authors: name, role, bio and photo
At least six to ten published pieces with title, dek, topic, author, dates and reading time
Cover images with alt text and photo credits
Issue structure if the publication runs issues (number, date, theme, contents)
Footnotes, figures, code samples or data tables in the pieces that need them
Newsletter promise and cadence; RSS feed

styles.name: bookish magazine
styles.why: Garamond-style headings over a screen serif, one ink-blue accent, wide margins for side notes. Suits essays, culture and long-form journalism.

styles.name: terminal log
styles.why: Dark by default with a reader light-mode switch, system type, mono dates and an amber accent; terse fades only. Suits engineering and developer blogs.

styles.name: clean newsroom
styles.why: Dense grotesk lists, brand accent for topics; for a company or team blog publishing often.

pitfalls: Images without real alt text or photo credits; covers reused across pieces.
Missing published and updated dates, author and reading time; these are also what search engines and readers look for.
Archive filters that reset on back / forward or cannot be linked; keep them in the URL and announce result counts.
Keyboard shortcuts that fire while typing in a field, or that are not documented on the page.
Code blocks that break the layout on phones; they must scroll inside their own box and stay readable in both themes.
Line length too long for reading; keep the body column near 60–75 characters.
Signup forms without consent wording or a privacy link.
